student_answer: OOP is about using classes and objects. It has inheritance and encapsulation. Inheritance allows reusing code from another class.
reference_answer: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm centered on objects containing data (attributes) and code (methods). The four fundamental principles are: 1. Encapsulation - bundling data and methods while restricting direct access. 2. Abstraction - hiding internal implementation complexity. 3. Inheritance - creating new classes based on existing classes to reuse code. 4. Polymorphism - allowing entities to take on different forms depending on context.
